rationale: B wins because it shows restraint: four viable desks, fewer padded swings, and sharper proof discipline. Its line, "Without at least the return rate, this angle is a question, not a story," is exactly the kind of sentence that keeps a founder from pitching vapor. A has strong bones, but "does the rest of the running category have to follow?" manufactures competitive stakes the update does not prove, and "retail-finance or markets reporter" reaches for a desk without the numbers that desk needs.
gaps_in_A: "does the rest of the running category have to follow?" overstates competitive pressure from one nationwide rollout; no competitors, analyst reaction, or adoption signal is in the update.
"retail-finance or markets reporter" is a stretch when the update withholds monthly price, unit economics, pilot scale, and any revenue materiality.
"moving a core product line to this model" overclaims. The facts support one shoe subscription, not a core product line shift.
The customer and category angles both orbit the same access-not-ownership hook; useful, but the set needs culling so altitude changes do not masquerade as new stories.
gaps_in_B: "this model hands the retirement decision to the brand" is invented. The update does not say who decides when a subscriber returns the shoe.
"The castor bean is quietly becoming a running-shoe raw material" turns one On product into a trend before proving broader adoption.
"The protagonist here is the input, not the brand" is smart, but it needs production volume fast; without it the materials angle becomes a curiosity, not a market signal.
"journalist-fit-check" is not quite the first operational step unless names already exist; the founder still needs a tightly sourced target list for the chosen desk.
